agyos_skill.intent: Behavioral guidelines to eliminate LLM coding mistakes. Use when writing, reviewing, or refactoring code to avoid overcomplication, make surgical changes, surface assumptions, and define verifiable success criteria.
agyos_skill.instructions: Behavioral engineering guidelines for AGYOS agents and operators, derived from Andrej Karpathy's findings on large language model coding failure modes. Tradeoff: These rules prioritize correctness and precision over rapid generation. For trivial one-line edits, apply pragmatic judgment. Surface assumptions, state uncertainties, and evaluate tradeoffs prior to mutation. Before writing code: - State technical assumptions explicitly in the implementation plan. When requirements admit multiple valid interpretations, list each option with its tradeoff rather than silently choosing one. - If a simpler design exists, present it directly. Push back against unnecessary abstractions or requirements that conflict with simplicity. - When an instruction is ambiguous, pause. Formulate one specific clarifying question rather than guessing. Deliver the minimal complete solution that directly satisfies the requirement. Implementation rules: - Build only the requested capabilities. Reject speculative extensions or hypothetical future requirements. - Never introduce helper classes, abstraction layers, or design patterns for single-use code. - Avoid artificial configurability or parameter sprawl that was not specified. - Keep functions under 50 lines with a single responsibility. - Keep source files under the 800-line maintainability ceiling. - If an implementation spans 200 lines where 50 lines suffice, refactor to the simpler 50-line implementation. Confine file mutations strictly to the task boundary. Editing rules: - Do not modify adjacent, unrelated code, comments, or formatting styles during a bug fix or feature addition. - Preserve working production code even if alternative syntax is preferred. - Match existing repository conventions, indentation, and architectural patterns. - If unrelated dead code is observed, report it in the summary rather than deleting it unprompted. - When new code makes an import, variable, or helper obsolete, remove that specific orphan immediately.
